alias.desc: Renames the output expression column key.

cast.desc: Coerces the column data type to another type.

debug.desc: Prints the current evaluation intermediate array to console for debugging.

all.desc: Creates an expression targeting all columns in the DataFrame.
all.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression targeting all columns.

coalesce.desc: Returns the first non-null value among the specified expressions.

params.name: exprs
params.desc: The list of expressions or columns to coalesce.

coalesce.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression resolving to the first non-null value.

duration.desc: Constructs a Duration expression column from numeric values, column references, or expressions.

params.name: [options]
params.desc: Duration component options (weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds, microseconds, nanoseconds, timeUnit).

duration.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression with the calculated duration values.

element.desc: Creates an expression referencing the current element(s) of an array during evaluation. Primarily used inside array operations like `filter`, `map`, or `eval`.
element.returns: {ColumnExpr<T>} A column expression referencing the array element.

exclude.desc: Creates an expression targeting all columns except the specified ones.

params.name: columns
params.desc: The name or names of columns to exclude.

exclude.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression targeting all columns except the specified ones.

implode.desc: Aggregates values of a column into a list within each group.

params.name: column
params.desc: The column or expression to implode.

implode.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression representing the list of values.

lit.desc: Creates a literal column expression that repeats the given value for all rows.

params.name: value
params.desc: The literal value (number, string, boolean, etc.).

params.name: [options]
params.desc: Configuration options.

params.name: [options.dtype]
params.desc: The data type to allocate for the literal values.

params.name: [options.name]
params.desc: The name of the output column.

lit.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression with the literal value.

seqRange.desc: Creates a column expression that generates a range of values. If mode is "cumulative" (default) or "independent", it generates a sequence. If mode is "constant", it repeats the given value.

params.name: value
params.desc: The initial value to start the sequence or the constant value to repeat.

params.name: [options]
params.desc: Configuration options.

params.name: [options.n]
params.desc: The number of values to generate. Defaults to the slice/DataFrame height.

params.name: [options.dtype]
params.desc: The registered data type to coerce/allocate for the generated sequence.

params.name: [options.name]
params.desc: The name of the output column.

params.name: [options.mode]
params.desc: The sequence generation mode ("constant", "cumulative", or "independent").

params.name: [options.step]
params.desc: The step value or function to compute the step at each row.

params.name: [options.strict]
params.desc: If true, throws an error if the generated sequence height does not match the target height.

params.name: [options.pad]
params.desc: In non-strict mode, pads the sequence with `padValue` if it is shorter than target range.

params.name: [options.truncate]
params.desc: In non-strict mode, truncates the sequence if it exceeds target range.

params.name: [options.padValue]
params.desc: The value to use for padding in non-strict mode.

params.name: [options.startIndex]
params.desc: The starting index in the DataFrame to insert the sequence.

params.name: [options.endIndex]
params.desc: The ending index in the DataFrame to insert the sequence.

seqRange.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression generating the sequence.

struct.desc: Packages multiple expressions into a structured object column.

params.name: fields

params.desc: Additional fields when a single expression is passed as the first parameter.

struct.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression packaging the specified fields.

$df.struct(

when.desc: Provides conditional branch evaluations inside column expressions.

params.name: predicate
params.desc: The boolean condition or expression.

when.returns: {WhenThenChain} A When object builder to chain `.then()` and `.otherwise()`/`.when()`.

all.desc: Aggregation: Returns true if all values in the group are truthy.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [true, true, false] })
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").all().alias("all_true"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌───────┬──────────┐
│ group │ all_true │
├───────┼──────────┤
│ "A"   │ true     │
│ "B"   │ false    │
└───────┴──────────┘

allNull.desc: Aggregation: Checks if all values in the group are null.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [null, null] })
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").allNull().alias("isNull"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬─────────┐
│ group │ isNull │
├───────┼─────────┤
│ "A"   │ true    │
└───────┴─────────┘

any.desc: Aggregation: Checks if any value in the group is truthy.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [true, false, false] })
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").any().alias("any_true"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌───────┬──────────┐
│ group │ any_true │
├───────┼──────────┤
│ "A"   │ true     │
│ "B"   │ false    │
└───────┴──────────┘

anyNull.desc: Aggregation: Checks if any value in the group is null.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [10, null] })
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").anyNull().alias("has_null"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬──────────┐
│ group │ has_null │
├───────┼──────────┤
│ "A"   │ true     │
└───────┴──────────┘

argMax.desc: Aggregation: Finds the index of the maximum value in the group.

argMin.desc: Aggregation: Finds the index of the minimum value in the group.

avg.desc: Aggregation: Computes the arithmetic mean of the group.

bitwiseAnd.desc: Aggregation: Computes bitwise AND across all elements in the group.

bitwiseOr.desc: Aggregation: Computes bitwise OR across all elements in the group.

bitwiseXor.desc: Aggregation: Computes bitwise XOR across all elements in the group.

corr.desc: Aggregation: Computes the Pearson correlation coefficient between two columns.

params.name: other
params.desc: The target column expression to correlate with.

count.desc: Aggregation: Returns the count of records inside the group.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [10, null] })
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").count().alias("cnt"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬─────┐
│ group │ cnt │
├───────┼─────┤
│ "A"   │ 1   │
└───────┴─────┘

params.name: options
params.desc: Config flags including whether to count null values.

cov.desc: Aggregation: Computes the covariance between two columns.

params.name: other
params.desc: The target column expression to compute covariance with.

dot.desc: Aggregation: Computes the dot product with another column.

params.name: other
params.desc: The other column expression to compute the dot product with.

entropy.desc: Aggregation: Computes the Shannon entropy of a column or group.

params.name: options
params.desc: Entropy options ({ base?: number, normalize?: boolean }, default base=Math.E, normalize=true).

first.desc: Aggregation: Finds the first value in the group.

implode.desc: Aggregation: Combines all values in the group into a single array/list cell.

kurtosis.desc: Aggregation: Computes the kurtosis (peakedness/tailedness) of a numeric column.

params.name: options
params.desc: Kurtosis calculation options ({ fisher?: boolean, bias?: boolean }, default fisher=true, bias=true).

last.desc: Aggregation: Finds the last value in the group.

max.desc: Aggregation: Finds the maximum value in the group.

maxBy.desc: Aggregation: Finds the value in this column corresponding to the maximum value in the `by` expression.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ name: ["a", "b", "c"], score: [10, 50, 20] })
>>> df.select($df.col("name").maxBy($df.col("score")).alias("top_scorer"))
shape: (1, 1)
┌────────────┐
│ top_scorer │
├────────────┤
│ "b"        │
└────────────┘

params.name: by
params.desc: Column or expression to order by.

mean.desc: Aggregation: Computes the arithmetic mean of elements in the group.

min.desc: Aggregation: Finds the minimum value in the group.

minBy.desc: Aggregation: Finds the value in this column corresponding to the minimum value in the `by` expression.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ name: ["a", "b", "c"], score: [10, 50, 20] })
>>> df.select($df.col("name").minBy($df.col("score")).alias("lowest_scorer"))
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────────────┐
│ lowest_scorer│
├──────────────┤
│ "a"          │
└──────────────┘

params.name: by
params.desc: Column or expression to order by.

mode.desc: Aggregation: Finds the statistical mode (most frequent value).

n_unique.desc: Aggregation: Computes number of unique elements.

params.name: options
params.desc: Uniqueness options.

nanMax.desc: Aggregation: Finds the maximum value in the group, taking NaN values into account (NaN propagates).
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [10, NaN] })
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").nanMax().alias("nan_max_val"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬─────────────┐
│ group │ nan_max_val │
├───────┼─────────────┤
│ "A"   │ NaN         │
└───────┴─────────────┘

nanMin.desc: Aggregation: Finds the minimum value in the group, taking NaN values into account (NaN propagates).
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [10, NaN] })
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").nanMin().alias("nan_min_val"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬─────────────┐
│ group │ nan_min_val │
├───────┼─────────────┤
│ "A"   │ NaN         │
└───────┴─────────────┘

null_count.desc: Aggregation: Counts the number of null or missing records.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [10, null] })
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").null_count().alias("nulls"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬───────┐
│ group │ nulls │
├───────┼───────┤
│ "A"   │ 1     │
└───────┴───────┘

quantile.desc: Aggregation: Computes the specific quantile values (0.0 to 1.0).

params.name: q
params.desc: The quantile parameter value between 0.0 and 1.0.

product.desc: Aggregation: Computes the product of all elements in the group.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [2, 5] })
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").product().alias("p"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬────┐
│ group │ p  │
├───────┼────┤
│ "A"   │ 10 │
└───────┴────┘

skew.desc: Aggregation: Computes the sample skewness as the Fisher-Pearson coefficient of skewness.

params.name: options
params.desc: Skew calculation options ({ bias?: boolean }, default bias=true).

spearman_corr.desc: Aggregation: Computes the Spearman rank correlation coefficient.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ x: [1, 2, 3], y: [5, 6, 7] })
>>> df.select($df.col("x").spearman_corr($df.col("y")).alias("spearman"))
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────────┐
│ spearman │
├──────────┤
│ 1        │
└──────────┘

params.name: other
params.desc: The other column expression to correlate with.

sum.desc: Aggregation: Computes the sum of elements in the group.

examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ val: [10, 20], weight: [1, 3] })
>>> df.select($df.col("val").w_avg($df.col("weight")).alias("w_mean"))
shape: (1, 1)
┌────────┐
│ w_mean │
├────────┤
│ 17.5   │
└────────┘

params.name: weights
params.desc: The weight values or column expression.

abs.desc: Computes the absolute value of the column values.

acos.desc: Computes the mathematical arccosine (inverse cosine) of the column values.

acosh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic arccosine of the column values.

add.desc: Adds a scalar value or another column expression.

params.name: val
params.desc: The number or column expression to add.

asin.desc: Computes the arcsine of the column values.

asinh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic arcsine of the column values.

atan.desc: Computes the arctangent of the column values.

atan2.desc: Computes the quadrant-aware arctangent of two values.

params.name: val
params.desc: The x denominator number or column expression.

atanh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic arctangent of the column values.

cbrt.desc: Computes the cube root of the column values.

ceil.desc: Rounds column values up to the nearest integer.

clip.desc: Clamps column values between lower and upper numeric thresholds.

params.desc: The lower threshold value (default: null).

params.name: upper
params.desc: The upper threshold value (default: null).

)

params.name: val
params.desc: The sign source value or column expression.

cos.desc: Computes the cosine of the column values.

cosh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic cosine of the column values.

degrees.desc: Converts angles from radians to degrees.

div.desc: Divides column values by a scalar or another column expression.

params.name: val
params.desc: The denominator value or column expression.

exp.desc: Computes natural exponent (e^x) of the column values.

expm1.desc: Computes e^x - 1 for each element in the column.

floor.desc: Rounds column values down to the nearest integer.

floordiv.desc: Performs integer division floor(x / y) on column values.

params.name: val
params.desc: The divisor value or column expression.

hypot.desc: Computes the hypotenuse sqrt(x^2 + y^2) of two values.

params.name: val

log.desc: Computes the logarithm of positive values with a specified base.

mod.desc: Computes modulo remainder (x % y) of column values.

params.desc: The multiplier value or column expression.

pow.desc: Raises column values to the specified power.

params.name: val
params.desc: The exponent power value or column expression.

radians.desc: Converts angles from degrees to radians.

sin.desc: Computes the sine of the column values.

sinh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic sine of the column values.

sqrt.desc: Computes the square root of non-negative column values.

sub.desc: Subtracts a scalar or another column expression.

tan.desc: Computes the tangent of the column values.

tanh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic tangent of the column values.

isInfinite.desc: Checks if values are positive or negative Infinity.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1.5, Infinity, -Infinity] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").isInfinite().alias("inf"))
shape: (3, 2)
┌───────────┬───────┐
│ a         │ inf   │
├───────────┼───────┤
│ 1.5       │ false │
│ Infinity  │ true  │
│ -Infinity │ true  │
└───────────┴───────┘

>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1.5, NaN] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").isNan().alias("nan"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬───────┐
│ a   │ nan   │
├─────┼───────┤
│ 1.5 │ false │
│ NaN │ true  │
└─────┴───────┘

isNotNan.desc: Checks if values are not NaN.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1.5, NaN] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").isNotNan().alias("not_nan"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬─────────┐
│ a   │ not_nan │
├─────┼─────────┤
│ 1.5 │ true    │
│ NaN │ false   │
└─────┴─────────┘

isNotNull.desc: Checks if column values are non-null and valid (not null, undefined, or missing).
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ email: ["alice@example.com", null] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("email").isNotNull().alias("valid"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌───────────────────┬───────┐
│ email             │ valid │
├───────────────────┼───────┤
│ alice@example.com │ true  │
│ null              │ false │
└───────────────────┴───────┘

isNull.desc: Checks if column values are null, undefined, or missing.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ email: ["alice@example.com", null] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("email").isNull().alias("missing"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌───────────────────┬─────────┐
│ email             │ missing │
├───────────────────┼─────────┤
│ alice@example.com │ false   │
│ null              │ true    │
└───────────────────┴─────────┘

isUnique.desc: Checks if values occur exactly once in the column.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 2] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").isUnique().alias("uniq"))
shape: (3, 2)

│ 1 │ true  │
│ 2 │ false │
│ 2 │ false │
└───┴───────┘

le.desc: Boolean comparison: Returns true if less than or equal to argument.

params.name: val
params.desc: The value or column expression to compare against.

lt.desc: Boolean comparison: Returns true if less than argument.

params.name: val
params.desc: The value or column expression to compare against.

ne.desc: Boolean comparison: Returns true if values do not match.

>>> const df = $df.data({ category: ["electronics", "toys"] })

└─────────────┴──────────┘

params.name: val
params.desc: The value or column expression to compare against.

neMissing.desc: Difference check that treats null values as equal to each other.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, null, 3] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").neMissing(null).alias("not_missing"))
shape: (3, 2)
┌──────┬─────────────┐
│ a    │ not_missing │
├──────┼─────────────┤
│ 1    │ true        │
│ null │ false       │
│ 3    │ true        │
└──────┴─────────────┘

params.name: val
params.desc: The value or column expression to compare against.

notIn.desc: Checks if values are not elements of a specific array or set list.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ category: ["toys", "books", "food"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("category").notIn(["toys", "books"]).alias("notIn"))
shape: (3, 2)
┌──────────┬────────┐
│ category │ notIn │
├──────────┼────────┤
│ toys     │ false  │
│ books    │ false  │
│ food     │ true   │
└──────────┴────────┘

params.name: values
params.desc: An array of candidate values or a single value to match against.

and.desc: Logical AND check supporting Kleene logic.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({
...   a: [true, true, false, null],
...   b: [true, false, false, true]
... })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").and($df.col("b")).alias("and_res"))
shape: (4, 3)
┌───────┬───────┬─────────┐
│ a     │ b     │ and_res │
├───────┼───────┼─────────┤
│ true  │ true  │ true    │
│ true  │ false │ false   │
│ false │ false │ false   │
│ null  │ true  │ null    │
└───────┴───────┴─────────┘

params.name: other
params.desc: The other boolean column expression or literal value to compare.

examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({
...   is_active: [true, false, null]
... })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("is_active").not().alias("is_inactive"))
shape: (3, 2)
┌───────────┬─────────────┐
│ is_active │ is_inactive │
├───────────┼─────────────┤
│ true      │ false       │
│ false     │ true        │
│ null      │ null        │
└───────────┴─────────────┘

or.desc: Logical OR check supporting Kleene logic.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({
...   a: [true, false, false, null],
...   b: [false, false, true, false]
... })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").or($df.col("b")).alias("or_res"))
shape: (4, 3)
┌───────┬───────┬────────┐
│ a     │ b     │ or_res │
├───────┼───────┼────────┤
│ true  │ false │ true   │
│ false │ false │ false  │
│ false │ true  │ true   │
│ null  │ false │ null   │
└───────┴───────┴────────┘

params.name: other
params.desc: The other boolean column expression or literal value to compare.

examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({
...   a: [true, true, false, false],
...   b: [true, false, true, false]
... })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").xor($df.col("b")).alias("xor_res"))
shape: (4, 3)
┌───────┬───────┬─────────┐
│ a     │ b     │ xor_res │
├───────┼───────┼─────────┤

│ true  │ false │ true    │
│ false │ true  │ true    │
│ false │ false │ false   │
└───────┴───────┴─────────┘

params.name: other
params.desc: The other boolean column expression or literal value to compare.

fillNull.desc: Replaces null, undefined, or missing values with a specified value or strategy.

params.name: options
params.desc: Configuration options including fill value, strategy ("forward", "backward", "zero", "one", "mean", "min", "max"), and optional limit.

reverse.desc: Reverses the order of values in the column.

concat.desc: Concatenates string elements with another string value or expression.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ first: ["John"], last: ["Doe"] })

shape: (1, 3)

│ first │ last │ full     │
├───────┼──────┼──────────┤

└───────┴──────┴──────────┘

params.name: other
params.desc: The string value or column expression to concatenate.

contains.desc: Checks if a string contains the search substring pattern (supports Regex).
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ email: ["user@example.com", "admin@test.org"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("email").str.contains("@example.com").alias("is_example"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌──────────────────┬────────────┐
│ email            │ is_example │
├──────────────────┼────────────┤
│ user@example.com │ true       │
│ admin@test.org   │ false      │
└──────────────────┴────────────┘

params.name: pattern
params.desc: The search substring or regular expression pattern.

containsAny.desc: Checks if a string contains any of the search patterns.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ email: ["user@example.com", "admin@test.org"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("email").str.containsAny(["@example.com", "@test.org"]).alias("is_target"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌──────────────────┬───────────┐
│ email            │ is_target │
├──────────────────┼───────────┤
│ user@example.com │ true      │
│ admin@test.org   │ true      │
└──────────────────┴───────────┘

params.name: patterns
params.desc: Array of substring or regular expression search patterns.

countMatches.desc: Counts occurrences of a substring or regular expression match in each string element.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ code: ["banana", "apple"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("code").str.countMatches("a").alias("a_count"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌────────┬─────────┐
│ code   │ a_count │
├────────┼─────────┤
│ banana │ 3       │
│ apple  │ 1       │
└────────┴─────────┘

params.name: pattern
params.desc: Search substring or regular expression.

escapeRegex.desc: Escapes special regular expression characters in string elements.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ pat: ["a.b", "c$d"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("pat").str.escapeRegex().alias("escaped"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌───────┬─────────┐
│ pat   │ escaped │
├───────┼─────────┤
│ a.b   │ a\.b    │
│ c$d   │ c\$d    │
└───────┴─────────┘

decode.desc: Decodes hex or base64 encoded string column values into string.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ encoded: ["68656c6c6f"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("encoded").str.decode({ encoding: "hex" }).alias("decoded"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌────────────┬─────────┐
│ encoded    │ decoded │
├────────────┼─────────┤
│ 68656c6c6f │ hello   │
└────────────┴─────────┘

params.name: options
params.desc: Object containing encoding ("hex" | "base64") and optional strict flag

encode.desc: Encodes string column values into hex or base64.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ text: ["hello"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("text").str.encode({ encoding: "hex" }).alias("encoded"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬────────────┐
│ text  │ encoded    │
├───────┼────────────┤
│ hello │ 68656c6c6f │
└───────┴────────────┘

params.name: options
params.desc: Object containing encoding ("hex" | "base64")

examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ url: ["hello%20world"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("url").str.decode_uri_component().alias("decoded"))
shape: (1, 2)

>>> const df = $df.data({ term: ["hello world"] })

├─────────────┼───────────────┤
│ hello world │ hello%20world │
└─────────────┴───────────────┘

endsWith.desc: Checks if string ends with a suffix.
examples:

shape: (2, 2)

└──────────────┴────────┘

params.desc: The suffix substring.

explode.desc: Splits strings into lists of single characters.

params.name: pattern
params.desc: The regex pattern containing capture groups.

params.name: options

extractAll.desc: Extracts all occurrences matching a regular expression pattern.

params.name: pattern
params.desc: Search pattern (string or RegExp).

params.name: options
params.desc: Options object. Use `groupIndex` to select the group (default 0).

params.name: pattern
params.desc: Search pattern containing capture groups.

extractMany.desc: Extracts the first regex match for each pattern in a list of patterns.

params.name: patterns
params.desc: Array of regular expression patterns or strings.

params.name: options
params.desc: Named options object ({ asciiCaseInsensitive, overlapping }).

find.desc: Return the byte offset of the first substring matching a pattern. Returns null if pattern is not found.

params.name: value
params.desc: Search string or regular expression.

params.name: options
params.desc: Configuration options ({ literal, asciiCaseInsensitive }).

findMany.desc: Return the starting byte offset of each match for multiple patterns.

>>> const df = $df.data({ text: ["user_123_PROD"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("text").str.findMany([/user_\d+/, /PROD/]).alias("positions"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────────────┬───────────┐
│ text          │ positions │
├───────────────┼───────────┤
│ user_123_PROD │ [0, 9]    │
└───────────────┴───────────┘

params.name: patterns
params.desc: Array of regular expressions or literal search strings.

params.name: options
params.desc: Configuration options ({ literal, asciiCaseInsensitive, overlapping, leftmost }).

head.desc: Extracts the first n characters of each string element.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ name: ["polars", "javascript"] })
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("name").str.head(3).alias("prefix"))
shape: (2, 2)

│ polars     │ pol    │
│ javascript │ jav    │
└────────────┴────────┘

params.name: n

join.desc: Joins a list of string elements into a single string using a delimiter. Accepts `JoinArrayOptions` (`{ ignoreNulls, nullValue, prefix, suffix, limit, truncationMarker, valueFormatter }`).

params.name: delimiter
params.desc: The string delimiter to join elements with.

params.name: options
params.desc: Formatting configuration options (`JoinArrayOptions`).

jsonDecode.desc: Decodes JSON string elements into parsed objects or arrays. Reuses safeJsonParse utility.

params.name: options
params.desc: Configuration options for parsing (`SafeJsonParseOptions`).

params.name: jsonPath

len.desc: Returns string length in UTF-16 code units. Alias for lenChars.

>>> const df = $df.data({ str: ["hello"] })

shape: (1, 2)

│ str   │ length │
├───────┼────────┤
│ hello │ 5      │
└───────┴────────┘

lenBytes.desc: Returns string length in UTF-8 encoded bytes.

lenChars.desc: Returns string length in character count.

└───────┴─────────┘

pad_start.desc: Pads start of strings to specified width. Alias for lpad.

params.name: width

params.name: fill
params.desc: Character sequence used for padding.

replace.desc: Replaces the first occurrence matching a string pattern.

params.desc: The search pattern string or regular expression.

params.desc: The search pattern string or regular expression.

params.name: replacement
params.desc: The replacement value.

replace_all.signature:

params.desc: Array of replacement strings/callbacks (when patterns is an array).

replaceMany.signature:
$df.col(<column_name>).str.replaceMany(

rpad.desc: Pads end of strings to specified width.

params.name: characters

DateTimeExprNamespace.desc:
**Implementation Notes**

_TimeUnit_: `Date` objects are always millisecond-based, so `timeUnit` is schema metadata only. Sub-millisecond precision (`us`, `ns`) cannot be stored; methods such as `microsecond()` and `nanosecond()` always scale from milliseconds. Migrating to raw `BigInt` arrays would be required for true sub-ms storage.

_Timezone enforcement_: `convertTimeZone` can only validate that the column is timezone-aware when `_castType` is explicitly set within the expression chain (e.g. after `castTimeUnit`). Enforcement against a column whose type is unknown at expression-build time requires schema-level checks in DataFrame operations.

Preserves the exact UTC epoch instant while changing the timezone label, affecting how local wall-clock component extractors (`hour()`, `day()`, etc.) and `strftime` interpret values. Requires the column to already be timezone-aware; use `replace({ timeZone })` to assign a timezone to a naive column first.

params.desc: Target IANA timezone identifier (e.g. `"UTC"`, `"America/New_York"`, `"Europe/London"`).

join.desc: Joins two DataFrames on key columns using a specified join strategy. - `"inner"` — Only rows with matching keys in both DataFrames. - `"left"` — All left rows; unmatched right values are `null`. - `"right"` — All right rows; unmatched left values are `null`. - `"outer"` — All rows from both sides; unmatched values are `null`. - `"semi"` — Left rows that have a match in the right DataFrame (only left columns retained). - `"anti"` — Left rows that have **no** match in the right DataFrame (only left columns retained). - `"cross"` — Cartesian product pairing every left row with every right row (keyless). non-key column names (default `["", "_right"]`). Ignored for `"semi"` and `"anti"` joins. across DataFrames. Default `false` (SQL-standard: `NULL != NULL`). - `"none"` (or `false`) — No specific ordering is desired. - `"left"` (or `true`) — Preserves the order of the left DataFrame. - `"right"` — Preserves the order of the right DataFrame. - `"left_right"` — Preserves the order of the left DataFrame first, then the right. - `"right_left"` — Preserves the order of the right DataFrame first, then the left.

joinAsof.desc:
Performs an asof (as-of) join for inexact matching on ordered numeric or temporal key columns.

Similar to a left join, but instead of exact key equality, matches the nearest key row from the right DataFrame according to the selected `strategy` ("backward", "forward", or "nearest") and optional `tolerance`. Both DataFrames must be sorted in ascending order on their respective `on` / `leftOn` / `rightOn` join keys.

- `"backward"` — Matches the latest right row where `rightKey <= leftKey`. - `"forward"` — Matches the earliest right row where `rightKey >= leftKey`. - `"nearest"` — Matches the right row with the absolute nearest key value to `leftKey`.

params.desc: Group column(s) for exact key matching in left DataFrame.

params.name: [options.rightBy]
params.desc: Group column(s) for exact key matching in right DataFrame.

params.name: [options.coalesce]
params.desc: Coalescing behavior for join key columns. Default `true`.

params.desc: Whether to verify that join keys are sorted ascending prior to matching. Default `true`.

concat.desc: Concatenates items vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.
examples:
// 1. Vertical Concatenation (default):
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ a: [1] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ a: [2] })
>>> $df.concat([df1, df2], { how: "vertical" })
shape: (2, 1)
┌───┐
│ a │
├───┤
│ 1 │
│ 2 │
└───┘

// 2. Horizontal Concatenation:
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ a: [1] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ b: [2] })
>>> $df.concat([df1, df2], { how: "horizontal" })
shape: (1, 2)
┌───┬───┐
│ a │ b │
├───┼───┤
│ 1 │ 2 │
└───┴───┘

// 3. Diagonal Concatenation (mismatched columns):
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ a: [1] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ b: [2] })
>>> $df.concat([df1, df2], { how: "diagonal" })
shape: (2, 2)
┌──────┬──────┐
│ a    │ b    │
├──────┼──────┤
│ 1    │ null │
│ null │ 2    │
└──────┴──────┘
